identity.short_description: A singlet fermion dark matter candidate odd under an approximate Z2^DM symmetry is produced by freeze-in through dimension-five operators, while a singlet scalar odd under Z2^DW forms domain walls whose annihilation is driven by quantum-gravity symmetry breaking.
identity.historical_origin_or_motivation: Introduced as a fermionic extension of an earlier scalar dark matter/domain-wall scenario to connect freeze-in dark matter, decays induced by quantum gravity, and gravitational waves from domain-wall annihilation.

additional_dark_sector_particles: singlet scalar S responsible for domain walls

dark_sector_couplings: dimension-five freeze-in interactions between singlet fermion, S, and H
QG-induced S-L-H operator causing neutrino mixing
interaction_operators: Z2-conserving dimension-five freeze-in operators suppressed by Lambda_FI
scalar potential with H^†H, S^2, H^†H S^2, and lambda_s(S^2-v_s^2)^2/4
QG bias operators S^5/Lambda_QG, S^3H^2/Lambda_QG, and S H^4/Lambda_QG
QG-breaking operator S chi L_i H/Lambda_QG in rendered notation
decay_channels: chi to photon plus active neutrino through mixing
chi to e+ e- plus active neutrino through weak interactions when kinematically allowed

eft_cutoff.name: freeze-in scale
eft_cutoff.notes: Dimension-five freeze-in operators are suppressed by Lambda_FI.

theory.notes: The EFT augments the Standard Model with a singlet fermion and singlet scalar, with approximate discrete symmetries broken by dimension-five QG-suppressed operators.

symmetries.stabilizing_mechanism: An approximate Z2^DM makes the singlet fermion long-lived, but QG-induced dimension-five operators break the symmetry and allow slow decays through mixing with active neutrinos.

symmetries.name: Z2^DM
symmetries.breaking: Explicitly broken by QG-suppressed dimension-five operators involving S, lepton doublets, and the Higgs.

symmetries.name: Z2^DW
symmetries.breaking: Spontaneously broken by the scalar S vev and explicitly biased by QG-suppressed operators, causing domain-wall annihilation.

breaking_scale.name: scalar vev
breaking_scale.notes: Benchmarks include v_s=10^10 GeV for relic-density illustration and v_s=2.21e6 GeV for a gravitational-wave example.

mechanisms: UV freeze-in from scattering through dimension-five operators
IR freeze-in from decays of s and h after symmetry breaking
production.notes: The paper emphasizes the singlet fermion never equilibrates with the thermal plasma and that the relic density is the sum of UV and IR freeze-in yields.

target_fraction.name: observed dark matter relic density
target_fraction.notes: Used for the solid relic-density contours in the T_RH-Lambda_FI and v_s-m_DM planes.

key_dependencies: Y_DM^IR from s and h decays

nonstandard_features: freeze-in production from a feebly coupled singlet fermion
spontaneous Z2^DW breaking creates domain walls
QG-induced bias makes domain walls annihilate before BBN in viable regions
dark matter can decay through active-neutrino mixing
phase_transitions: S obtains a vev and breaks Z2^DW
electroweak symmetry breaking induces scalar and neutrino mixing effects

phase_space.notes: Freeze-in production implies a nonthermal distribution, but the paper uses yield-level relic-density calculations rather than a full phase-space function.

core.name: dark matter mass
core.description: Mass of the singlet fermion dark matter candidate.
core.notes: Figures discuss examples from MeV to TeV scales.

core.name: freeze-in scale
core.description: Suppression scale for dimension-five operators that produce the FIMP abundance.
core.notes: The observed relic density fixes relations in the T_RH-Lambda_FI plane.

core.name: quantum-gravity breaking scale
core.description: Effective scale suppressing discrete-symmetry-breaking operators.
core.notes: The paper treats this as a free parameter constrained by decays and domain-wall gravitational waves.

core.name: scalar vev
core.description: Vacuum expectation value of S that breaks Z2^DW and enters the neutrino-mixing and domain-wall sectors.
core.notes: Benchmarks include 10^10 GeV for relic-density plots and 2.21e6 GeV for a NANOGrav-like example.

core.name: reheating temperature
core.description: Highest temperature controlling UV freeze-in production.
core.value: greater than O(MeV), up to about 10^16
core.notes: The text treats T_RH as a free parameter after discussing BBN and inflationary considerations.

core.name: scalar mass benchmark
core.description: Mass of the scalar excitation used in freeze-in examples.
core.notes: Used for demonstration in the relic-density contours.

nuisance.name: Higgs-singlet portal coupling
nuisance.description: Assumed small so S-Higgs mixing is negligible for v_s much larger than v_h.

nuisance.name: QG operator coefficients
nuisance.description: Dimensionless coefficients of QG-suppressed breaking operators, taken order one by redefining Lambda_QG.

derived.name: active-neutrino mixing angle
derived.description: Mixing of chi with active neutrinos after S and H get vevs.
derived.value: sum_i alpha_i v_s v_h /(2 Lambda_QG m_DM)
derived.notes: This mixing allows slow dark matter decays.

derived.name: total freeze-in yield
derived.description: Sum of UV and IR freeze-in contributions.

validity_domain.condition: The singlet fermion interactions must be weak enough that it never thermalizes with the Standard Model bath.
caveats: Larger couplings would invalidate the FIMP freeze-in treatment.

validity_domain.condition: The analysis assumes v_s much larger than v_h and lambda_hs sufficiently small so S-Higgs mixing is negligible.
caveats: Large mixing would change production and phenomenology.

validity_domain.condition: All relevant discrete-symmetry-breaking dimension-five operators are assumed to be suppressed by a common Lambda_QG with order-one coefficients.
caveats: Different QG scales for different operators would weaken the decay/GW correlation.

global.description: The Refined Swampland Global Symmetry Conjecture selects the lowest allowed dimension-five symmetry-breaking operators.
global.impact_if_violated: The correlated dark matter decay and domain-wall bias predictions could be absent or much smaller.

global.description: Dimensionless coefficients of QG-breaking operators are taken to be order one after redefining Lambda_QG.
global.impact_if_violated: Mixing angles, decay rates, and domain-wall annihilation scales would shift.

global.description: The reheating temperature is treated as a free parameter within broad cosmological bounds.
global.impact_if_violated: UV freeze-in abundance contours would change.

dominant_uncertainties: effective QG scale and order-one coefficients
relative UV versus IR freeze-in contribution
assumption of common symmetry-breaking scale
robustness.notes: The paper provides analytic yield formulae and benchmark plots; this extraction records text-supported model structure and dependencies.

warnings.warning: The Z2^DM symmetry is approximate and deliberately broken by QG operators; do not treat the fermion as exactly stable.
warnings.mitigation: Retain the QG-induced mixing and decay logic when using the model.

warnings.warning: The relic abundance can be dominated by UV or IR freeze-in depending on reheating and symmetry-breaking scales.
warnings.mitigation: Use the total yield Y_DM^UV+Y_DM^IR and avoid applying a single-regime approximation outside its stated domain.

source_chunks_or_sections.quote_or_summary: The paper extends a scalar DM/domain-wall scenario to fermionic FIMP dark matter with QG-broken discrete symmetries.
The model adds singlet S and singlet fermion chi, writes dimension-five freeze-in/QG operators, and computes UV plus IR freeze-in yields.

unresolved_items: The source text rendering drops some fermion symbols in the Lagrangian, so operator names are described conservatively.

caveats: Rendered text loses some symbols in the dimension-five Lagrangian, so the operator extraction is intentionally descriptive rather than algebraically exact.
